title: A Generalized quantum Stein lemma on von Neumann algebras
abstract: We prove a generalized quantum Stein lemma for i.i.d. normal states against convex, tensor-stable families on arbitrary von Neumann algebras. Assuming the existence of an alternative state with finite relative entropy from the null state, we show that, at every type-I error tolerance $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$, the worst case type-II error exponent is achieved with the regularized relative entropy with a strong converse. The proof combines the integral representation of relative entropy by hockey-stick divergences, a modular testing bound, and convex minimax argument.
summary: This theoretical paper generalizes the quantum Stein lemma to arbitrary von Neumann algebras, providing rigorous bounds for distinguishing between quantum states. It proves that the rate of distinguishability is governed by the regularized relative entropy, establishing a sharp threshold for testing quantities. This extends fundamental results from finite quantum systems to the most general setting of operator algebras.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove a generalized quantum Stein lemma for hypothesis testing involving i.i.d. normal states against convex, tensor-stable families on arbitrary von Neumann algebras.
main_result: It establishes that the asymptotic worst-case type-II error exponent is achieved by the regularized relative entropy, providing a strong converse for the distinguishability rate.
method: The proof combines integral representations of relative entropy (via hockey-stick divergences), a modular testing bound, and convex minimax arguments.
